name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,388

clue.text: Group of around 50 states regret over wish to leave here, initially?

indicators.note: something turned over ends up facing the other way, so the word for regret is flipped
the first letter of the word here is told to depart from the word for wish
points at only the opening letter of here as the one that goes

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
a hope is a wish
the first letter of here

explanation.surface: A post-referendum musing: regretting the wish to leave a fifty-member bloc, with Brexit in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the European Union, but the definition is the whole continent with its roughly fifty sovereign countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent contains around fifty sovereign countries, so a group of about fifty nations describes it.

clue.text: Stress as he is worried about rise of Theresa May

indicators.note: in a down answer a rise reads from the bottom upwards, so the title is turned round
worried means agitated and disturbed, so those three words are jumbled
about means the jumbled letters go round the turned title

blocks.note: taken as written
Theresa May was the UK Prime Minister, the PM

explanation.surface: A man is anxious about Theresa May's rise to power, and feeling the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May became Britain's Prime Minister in 2016. 'Stress' is a noun here, as in placing stress on a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is special importance or weight placed on something, which is what stress means in speech or argument.

clue.text: Religious Education likely to be well grounded

blocks.note: RE is the British school subject Religious Education
liable to do something means likely to do it

explanation.surface: A comment that a school's religious education lessons will probably have solid foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the school subject name in Britain, written out in full here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reliable is dependable and trustworthy, resting on a sound basis, which is what well grounded suggests.

clue.text: One's given a chair for female - terribly sore, clutching bottom in distress

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its final letter, so only the last of distress is used
terribly means badly, so the letters of sore are scrambled
clutching means holding inside, so the scrambled letters grip the single letter

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written
the last letter of distress

explanation.surface: A woman, painfully sore and in distress, is offered a seat to sit on.
explanation.walkthrough: The chair is not furniture but an academic post: a university chair is a professorship.
explanation.definitionFit: A university chair is a senior academic post, and the person appointed to it holds the title of professor.

clue.text: About to return money? Editor's stressed

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the short word for about is read backwards

blocks.note: ca. is circa, about
a cent is a coin of money
the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone is about to get their money back, and an editor is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Editor's stressed' reads as a stressed-out editor, but 's here is just 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An accented syllable is one given emphasis in speech, the same as a stressed syllable.

clue.text: Caught dace on Trent when spinning intensified

indicators.note: spinning means whirling round, so the fish and river letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: C is caught in cricket scoring
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler on the River Trent lands a dace using a spinning lure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major English river and a dace a small freshwater fish; 'spinning' is an angling method and also the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentrated means made stronger or more focused, which is what intensified describes.

clue.text: Former lover capsizing craft, unusually

indicators.note: a capsizing boat turns upside down, so in a down answer the word for craft is read upwards

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
craft means skill or art

explanation.surface: An ex-partner unexpectedly overturns a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat to go with capsizing; it means skill. Extra as an adverb means more than usually, as in extra careful.
explanation.definitionFit: Used before an adjective, extra means to an exceptional degree, so an extra large one is unusually large.

clue.text: Sport journalists in Netherlands locked up?

indicators.note: something locked is shut inside, so the letters are concealed within these words
in a down answer up means the concealed letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of journalists, the whole of in, and the start of Netherlands

explanation.surface: A question whether reporters in the Netherlands have been imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits backwards inside 'journalists in Netherlands'; 'in' looks like a link but is part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket game played over a net, a well-known sport.

clue.text: Colouring's fading, it's reported

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so what is wanted is a word that sounds like the one for fading

blocks.note: a fading thing is dying away

explanation.surface: A rumour that some dyed fabric is losing its colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colouring's' looks like a possessive noun; it is the verb form plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyeing is the act of changing the colour of fabric or hair with a stain.

clue.text: Paleness from friend left in front of soldiers

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
L is the abbreviation for left
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A friend left ahead of the troops, and somebody has gone pale.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, Other Ranks, is the crossword stand-by for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallor is an unhealthy whiteness of the face, which is exactly what paleness describes.

clue.text: Batting posture, for example

blocks.note: a batter in cricket who is batting is said to be in
a stance is a way of standing, a posture

explanation.surface: A cricket coach describes the way a batsman stands at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'. The surface makes 'for example' look like a throwaway, but 'example' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration, which is what an example is.

clue.text: Salesman feeling bitter about exhibiting

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
to resent something is to feel bitter about it

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman is aggrieved about having to display his goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' belongs to the wordplay phrase rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent can mean to depict or display, so representing a scene is exhibiting it.

clue.text: Come to a king in terror

indicators.note: in places the article and the monarch inside the word for terror

blocks.note: taken as written
K is king in chess notation
awe is fearful dread

explanation.surface: A king in a state of terror comes round, as if waking from a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to' is a phrasal verb, to regain consciousness, and awake works as a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to recover consciousness, and to awake is to rouse from sleep: both mean surfacing.

clue.text: Promotion? No - leave it out!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order and set down afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told they won't get a promotion and should drop the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave it out!' is London slang for 'stop it' or 'come off it', which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation is a raising in rank or position, so a step up the ladder is a promotion.

clue.text: Shows poorly American costs after start of treatment

indicators.note: start of takes only the opening letter of the word treatment
after puts the word for costs following the opening letter of treatment

blocks.note: poorly means unwell
US is an abbreviation for American
the first letter of treatment
rates are charges or costs

explanation.surface: An American patient falls ill and is hit by medical bills after starting treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows poorly' reads as 'performs badly', but 'poorly' is wordplay, an adjective meaning sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate something is to demonstrate or make it clear, much as one shows it.

clue.text: Reach hospital department on this?

blocks.note: to stretch is to reach out
ER is the Emergency Room, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A question of how a casualty gets to the emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: patients reach casualty lying on one. ER is the American emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a frame for carrying a sick or injured person lying down, often to emergency care.

clue.text: Fully entitled to leave 50% with bank

indicators.note: half of the word departs, so only its first four letters stay

blocks.note: taken as written
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Someone completely within their rights to walk out with half the bank's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the place that holds money; here it is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely means wholly or completely, which is the sense of fully.

clue.text: Remote island - nothing to get criticised about

indicators.note: about means the word for criticised wraps round the round letter

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
to slate is to criticise harshly
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A faraway island where there is nothing to complain about.
explanation.walkthrough: Slate is a British word for criticising severely, as in a play slated by reviewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated stands far apart from others, which is what remote means.

clue.text: Unrest as art's circulated, where you'll find plenty of scoffing

definitions.text: where you'll find plenty of scoffing

indicators.note: circulated means passed round and round, so the letters are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Controversial art goes on tour and is met with widespread mockery and jeering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffing' looks like mockery of the art; it is the British slang for eating greedily. The 's of art's is 'is', not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurants are places where people eat, and to scoff in British slang is to gobble food greedily.

clue.text: Frank regularly warned when caught by detectives

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of warned is kept
caught by means held by, so the kept letters sit inside the police department

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of warned
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A man named Frank keeps being warned and is finally arrested by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name; it is the adjective meaning honest and open.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means honest and straightforward in speech, just as frank does.

clue.text: Might heads of security come to be taken in by drug smuggler?

indicators.note: heads are the first letters of the two words that follow
taken in by means swallowed inside, so the smuggler word goes around the two letters

blocks.note: the first letters of security and come
a mule is someone who carries drugs across a border

explanation.surface: A question whether airport security might be fooled by a drug courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' opens the clue as if it were the verb of a question; it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means physical power or strength, which is the noun sense of might.

clue.text: Host a ball after food

indicators.note: after says the word for a ball comes following the word for food

blocks.note: taken as written
a bun is a piece of food
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone is told to throw a ball once the dinner has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a verb, to entertain guests, but it is a noun meaning a great number.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a large crowd or multitude, and abundance likewise is a great quantity.

clue.text: What's at the bottom of the bottle, for example, doctor's swallowed

definitions.text: What's at the bottom of the bottle

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so the abbreviation for for example goes into the doctor's word

blocks.note: DR is doctor, and 's adds the S
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A doctor downs the sediment at the bottom of a medicine bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of doctor's supplies the final S rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment left at the bottom of a wine bottle or glass after pouring.

clue.text: Pilot's path - one moving west

indicators.note: one is the letter I, and moving west shifts it a step to the left within the word for path

blocks.note: a trail is a path

explanation.surface: An airline pilot describes a flight path heading westward.
explanation.walkthrough: One is I. In an across answer west is leftwards, so the I in TRAIL moves one place left to give TRIAL. 'Pilot' is a noun: a test run.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot scheme is an experimental run before the real thing, which is what a trial is.

clue.text: Harry cried - pet's old and feeble

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy called Harry weeps because his beloved pet has grown old and frail.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a boy's name crying over his pet; it is a verb, to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes someone or something worn out and weakened by age.

clue.text: Warning from nurse outside hospital

indicators.note: outside means the word for nurse wraps around the hospital abbreviation

blocks.note: to nurse a patient is to treat them
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A nurse standing outside the hospital issues a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' looks like a noun, a person, but it is used as a verb, to treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a menacing warning that harm may follow.

clue.text: Time to follow groom? Horse is prepared for it

indicators.note: to follow places the word for time after the word for groom

blocks.note: to dress hair or a horse is to groom it
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A stable groom gets a horse ready for a show, and it's time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is a verb here. The definition is cryptic: a horse is trained, prepared, for this equestrian discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the competitive equestrian discipline of precise schooled movements, which a horse must be specially trained to perform.

clue.text: Look after piano, Edward's implored

indicators.note: after places the word for look following the musical abbreviation

blocks.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
in older English a ray is a glance or line of sight from the eye
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward begs someone to look after his piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as 'take care of', but the two words split: 'Look' is the wordplay and 'after' places it behind P. Ray for look is an old sense, a glance of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray in the older sense is to beg or entreat someone earnestly, so prayed means implored.
